title: Scalar flow_lift_factor is inverted: lifting water hotter RAISES COP (up to 2.02x), breaking batch parity
claim: ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor returns max(0.25, carnot_ref/carnot_flow), which is >1 for every flow above the 35 degC reference, so compute_cop (valve plant, direct-plant curve) and compute_cop_dhw rise with flow/tank temperature on every climate, while the batch twin _batch_cop applies carnot_flow/carnot_ref.
mechanism: The ratio of two Carnot COPs is inverted in the scalar law only. carnot_flow < carnot_ref above the reference, so ref/flow > 1: a 55 degC hot-water charge is priced at 1.34-1.61x the space COP instead of 0.62-0.75x, a throttled buffer at the tank temperature likewise, and the Carnot fraction of the priced COP exceeds 1 (a COP above the Carnot limit) on 21320 grid points in four of five climates. _batch_cop uses carnot_flow/carnot_ref, so scalar and batch disagree by up to 8.01 COP units on the same inputs.

evidence.unit: count of adjacent (flow or tank) grid pairs where COP rises with flow, over 5 climates
evidence.machine: box B5 (shared compute box, linux x86_64, venv-ci python 3.14)
evidence.contention_note: counts only; box shared with up to two other seats

perturbation.change: thermal_model.py flow_lift_factor: `return max(0.25, carnot_ref / carnot_flow)` -> `return max(0.25, carnot_flow / carnot_ref)` (harness --perturb=lift, private copy)

metric_definition: Count of adjacent grid pairs (flow 20-70 degC step 0.5, tank 35-65, outdoor = climate range +-2 K, 241 pts) where compute_cop(valve) or compute_cop_dhw rises as flow rises, tol 1e-12.
phenomenon_property: Every flow/tank lift factor that prices COP is a derate in [0.25, 1] that is non-increasing in flow temperature, and scalar and batch COP laws agree bitwise on the same inputs.
proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor: invert the ratio to carnot_flow/carnot_ref (the batch twin's form); every DHW and valve golden fixture drifts.
